thread:
sasha: Quick heads-up — q6b-int4 canary showed promptset drift between 'silo-A' and 'silo-B'. overlap up to 22% on embedding fingerprint. Thinking we should temporarily silo incoming ingest and run anchor cycling so labelers don't see duplicates. Sample stats: overlap=0.22, golden-fail=3/150.

ben: Can you post the query you used to measure overlap?

sasha: Sure:
```
SELECT fingerprint, count(*) FROM samplebank WHERE silo IN ('A','B') GROUP BY fingerprint HAVING count>1 LIMIT 50;
```
Overlap rows attached (short list). Need to decide: 1) immediate siloing + holdout of duplicates to avoid labeler fatigue, 2) run anchor cycling (rotate last 20% of anchors every 6 hrs), or 3) add dedupe pass in ingest.

maya: Option 1 seems fastest. How bad is labeler churn if we don't? We saw repeated labels cause golden flips last week.

sasha: Labeler queue shows 18% repeat hits for same prompt across buckets; predicted relabel cost ≈ 1200 labels/day.

james: If we silo, can we still keep goldlet exposure? I prefer anchor cycling + micro-golden refresh every 12 hrs.

ben: For canary bring-up, we should also compare q6b-int4 vs int8 baseline for generation diffs. I'll run a small eval on the overlapping set.

reno-bot: deploy-canary: q6b-int4 -> started 1718877805. will notify on completion.

maya: ok set plan: silo ingest for next 24h, anchor cycle 6h, micro-golden refresh 12h, ben to run overlap eval. james to update labeler instructions to skip exact-fingerprint duplicates (de-dup policy v0.3). sasha will post overlap CSV.

ben: ack. I'll attach eval summary when done.

sasha: thanks — will follow up with a short doc + task list. :thumbsup:
